subject: Biology
description: Phyla, classes — mammals, reptiles, fish, invertebrates

questions.stem: The largest phylum in the animal kingdom — accounting for over 80% of all known animal species — is:
questions.explanation: Arthropoda — insects, crustaceans, arachnids, myriapods — > 1.2 million described species, by far the largest phylum. Chordata (vertebrates + a few close relatives) has ~70,000 species. Mollusca (snails, squids, octopuses) ~85,000. Annelida (segmented worms) ~15,000. Characteristic arthropod features — exoskeleton (chitin), jointed appendages, segmented body.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Whales, dolphins and porpoises are members of the class:
questions.explanation: Despite looking like fish, whales, dolphins and porpoises are mammals — warm-blooded, breathe air, give birth to live young, produce milk, have hair at some stage of life. They belong to the order Cetacea. The blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus) is the largest living animal ever known — up to ~30 m long. Bats — another group of flying mammals (order Chiroptera).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Spiders and scorpions belong to which class of arthropods?
questions.explanation: Arachnids — 8 legs, 2 body parts (cephalothorax + abdomen), no antennae, no wings. Spiders, scorpions, mites, ticks. Insects — 6 legs, 3 body parts, antennae, usually wings. Crustaceans — 10-14 legs, 2 pairs of antennae, chiefly aquatic (crabs, lobsters, shrimps). Myriapoda — centipedes (1 pair of legs / segment) and millipedes (2 pairs / segment).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: An amphibian is an animal that:

options.option_text: Lives both on land and in water
Is warm-blooded and gives live birth

questions.explanation: Amphibia — cold-blooded vertebrates that lay eggs in water, spend part of life in water (as larvae — tadpoles) and part on land (as adults). Frogs, toads, salamanders, caecilians. Skin is moist and thin, allowing gas exchange. Reptiles (distinct from amphibians) have scaly skin and lay shelled eggs on land; mammals are warm-blooded and give live birth.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Match the animal with its phylum. A. Earthworm. B. Jellyfish. C. Octopus. D. Sea urchin. List-II: 1. Annelida, 2. Cnidaria, 3. Mollusca, 4. Echinodermata.
questions.explanation: Annelida — segmented worms (earthworm, leech). Cnidaria — jellyfish, hydra, coral, sea anemones (stinging cells). Mollusca — soft-bodied, often with shell — snails, squids, octopuses, oysters. Echinodermata — spiny-skinned marine animals (sea urchin, sea star, sea cucumber). Other major phyla — Porifera (sponges), Platyhelminthes (flatworms), Nematoda (roundworms), Chordata (vertebrates).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Snakes, lizards, crocodiles and turtles all belong to the class:
questions.explanation: Reptilia — cold-blooded vertebrates with dry, scaly skin that lay shelled eggs on land (amniotes). Snakes, lizards, crocodiles, alligators, turtles, tortoises. The king cobra (Ophiophagus hannah) is the world's longest venomous snake. Aves (birds) — warm-blooded, feathered descendants of dinosaurs and are, in strict cladistic taxonomy, a specialised branch of 'reptiles', but school taxonomy keeps them separate.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Invertebrates — animals that lack a vertebral column — make up roughly what fraction of all known animal species?
questions.explanation: Vertebrates (mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish) are a small minority — ~70,000 species out of ~1.5 million described animals. About 95 % of all described animal species are invertebrates, and most of those are arthropods (chiefly insects). Insects alone outnumber vertebrates roughly 15:1 in described species.
